title: Ship meeting recorder as installable PWA on existing Node server, not Electron
context: Need one locally installed app that records Zoom/Google Meet audio (system audio plus mic) and transcribes each recording with the existing local Whisper worker, with a persistent history.
decision: Package the app as an installable PWA served by the existing Node server on http://localhost:5000. The server autostarts hidden at Windows login, and the installer adds a desktop shortcut. Electron was rejected for now because it is slower to ship.
consequences: Recording uses Chrome getDisplayMedia for system/tab audio, so the Record tab depends on Chrome.
The server must run on localhost:5000 and autostart at Windows login (Startup folder).
Recordings are stored as files on disk (default %USERPROFILE%\Documents\Meeting Recordings, overridable via RECORDINGS_DIR); deletes move to _deleted\ so they are recoverable.
Installer scripts are Windows-only; non-Windows install scripts and Electron packaging are out of scope.
Transcription runs as a server background job that survives the HTTP request and keeps the source file.
